scope: Local generic schema refactor; no version bump, push, tag, release or hardware qualification.

identity_contract.reserved_types: Exact SDK protocol names and IDs 0–18 only.
identity_contract.reserved_endpoints: Exact SDK protocol names and IDs 200–202 only.
identity_contract.application_default: Namespace-specific stable name hash, independent of registration order and schema subset. Former application/test names have no special IDs.
identity_contract.explicit_id: Optional JSON u32 in runtime streaming and snapshot loaders, embedded flash generation, legacy proc macro and editor validation. Explicit IDs must be consistent across participants.
identity_contract.collision_behavior: Reject reserved spoofing and conflicting real identity claims before publication. Failed JSON loads and fallible merges retain previous definitions. Unclaimed ENDPOINT_<id> placeholders may learn real names.
identity_contract.protocol_metadata: Remote schemas cannot override SDK protocol metadata. Legacy macro protocol names, IDs, priorities, reliability, elements and endpoints match runtime definitions.
identity_contract.generated_mirrors: src/schema_identity.rs is authoritative. Explicit developer sync generates the standalone macro mirror and Python resolver. CI equality checks detect drift; ordinary builds never rewrite source files.

generic_routing.change: Removed three application HEARTBEAT routing exceptions for fanout, ACK suppression and shortest paths. Equal metadata and routes now have equal behavior under arbitrary application names. Managed-variable owner routing remains.
generic_routing.side_names: Production side labels do not select codecs, MTUs or routing priority. Actual transport profiles and configured capabilities remain legitimate protocol properties.

focused_validation.baseline_negative: Old HEARTBEAT implicit ID 106 fails the uniform hash regression.

default_unit_tests.environment: Explicit legacy test schema paths, matching build.py.

hosted_no_std.cases: One cached-transit, two identity and three schema-memory cases. Compiled explicit-ID flash catalog and runtime JSON agree; reserved-ID failure leaves state unchanged.

cases: Exact application wire chunks under RADIO, SD_CARD, SOFTWARE_BUS, IMU, GPS and arbitrary side labels
Opaque application IDs 19/50/99 and endpoint IDs 0/100/101 roundtrip without protocol privilege
Placeholder learning followed by rejection of conflicting real claims

macro_crate.includes: All protocol ID vectors and ordinary application-name hashes

focused_validation.clippy: All targets, -D warnings, passed; no lint allows added.
focused_validation.format: Root and macro crate rustfmt plus generated-mirror equality passed.

fixtures: Historical application IDs are explicit JSON test configuration, never a core name table.
memory_test_isolation: The existing hosted no_std zero-RAM case raced another case that retained 222 bytes of metadata. Each case now executes in a fresh child process with original assertions intact.
compatibility: Default application IDs and old ordinal macro discriminants change. Applications must configure legacy IDs before pinning this candidate. The version/release decision remains with the parent and user.
remaining: Full build.py test --all --full before any push, including the subsequent shared Router/Relay implementation
Matched all-seven TLSF+compact-ON builds and normal/mixed mode command, freshness and DAQ qualification
User owns crates.io/PyPI publication; release automation and version changes remain pending
